correctness.rationale: For every prime power q, direct UT_4 matrix multiplication gives three necessary and sufficient commutation equations aD=dA, dF=fD and aE+bF=Ae+Bf. On d!=0, the (r=a/d,s=f/d,t=r(e/d)-s(b/d)) labels partition the q(q²−1) nonzero directions into commuting fibers of size (q−1)q², plus one exceptional zero-direction fiber of size (q−1)q³; all distinct fibers are mutually noncommuting. On d=0 and (a,f)!=(0,0), projectivization identifies the noncommuting choices with pairwise nonorthogonal points of W(3,q) outside the isotropic line L:a=f=0; each has q(q−1) independent lifts. These two strata are completely cross-noncommuting. The residual stratum d=a=f=0 cannot meet the bound because it loses q(q−1)+1 eligible d!=0 fibers. Thus every maximizer and its multiplicity are exactly the displayed product in terms of beta_q and h_q. In W(3,3) a fresh exhaustive 40-point nonorthogonality recursion finds precisely 2880 size-seven partial ovoids, none larger, of which 864 avoid L; 864*6^7*18^24*54=2^37*3^61 and alpha_3=32. The all-q multiplicity is a parameterization, NOT a numeric evaluation of beta_q/h_q for every q. This finite check corroborates only the q=3 part.

value.rationale: Counting all maximum pairwise noncommuting subsets, rather than their size alone, is a natural exact invariant of a standard finite nilpotent matrix group. The symplectic partial-ovoid bijection and independent lift-factorization describe equality geometry for all field characteristics, and the fully evaluated ternary result is a motivated first nontrivial finite field. It is not a new determination of the known independence number or the 2880 partial ovoids, nor an unmotivated arbitrary slice.
